translations.10: The area of a Space that everyone can see is called the "Commons."
translations.11: Anyone can post notes to the Commons.
translations.12: Takanashi shares the sales schedule in the Commons every morning.
translations.13: You can invite members to a Space by email.
translations.14: The person you invite receives a confirmation email.
translations.15: Once an admin approves, they can join right away.
translations.16: You can also change members' permissions for each Commons.
translations.18: Notes are saved automatically and synced to all of your devices.
translations.19: You can edit offline, and changes sync as soon as you reconnect.
translations.2: Memotto is a note app that keeps your text, tables and images in one place.
translations.20: You can return to an earlier state from a page's Revisions.
translations.21: Yamanashi recovered a passage that had been deleted by mistake.
translations.23: It's handy to pin the pages that matter most.
translations.24: Pinned pages are listed at the top.
translations.25: Notes in the Commons are easier to find once you add tags.
translations.27: Takanashi uses a separate tag for each deal.
translations.28: The same tags work on Quick Notes too.
translations.29: Search covers both the Commons and Quick Notes at once.
translations.3: This guide uses two examples: Yamanashi from PR and Takanashi from sales.
translations.30: If you can't find something, try widening your search.
translations.4: A short note attached to a page is called a "Quick Note."
translations.5: Yamanashi keeps meeting decisions in Quick Notes.
translations.6: Yamanashi marks the important spots with Stickies.
translations.7: You can add up to ten Quick Notes to each page.
translations.9: Takanashi's sales team began by creating a Space.
